newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Alliance to set post-election requirements.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Alliance to set post-election requirements.

text.p: Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Tuesday his party would issue a briefing paper the day after the New Zealand general election setting out its minimum policy requirements for any parties wishing to form a government.
"What we are going to do is prepare a briefing paper for parties that want to be an incoming government," Anderton told a public meeting in Kelston, in the Waitakere electorate.
The Alliance would publish the requirements and the answers to them.

"We will be briefing them on how we see New Zealand society, the New Zealand economy, and what the minimum requirements are to get Alliance support ... and we will want to drive the hardest bargains on those things as we possibly can in the interest of New Zealand," Anderton said.
Anderton reiterated the Alliance would not support the governing National Party, nor would it give any party a "blank cheque" to do whatever it wished.
If planned legislation from any party did not meet the Alliance's minimum requirements, it would vote against it.
"We want good things to be done by parliament and bad things to be stopped from being done. The only way you can really do that is to have parliament govern, not Cabinet," he said.
Anderton said the plan to publish the Alliance requirements would mean no more secret "behind closed doors" negotiations.
"You will know why we are supporting a government, of whatever persuasion, or why we are not," he said.
"So those people who think the election finishes and all trials and tribulations are over on October 12, the real initiatives for New Zealand start on October 13," he said.

Earlier, Labour leader Helen Clark said she did not see the "slightest prospect" of a coalition with the left wing Alliance, but that she believed the Alliance would offer support on key policies to a Labour-led government after the election.
